name: Domperidone
executiveSummary: Peripheral prokinetic/antiemetic. Adult: **10 mg PO up to 3 times/day** (max **30 mg/day**, short courses). Pediatrics: restricted (QT); if used **0.25 mg/kg up to 3/day**. Avoid with long QT/potent CYP3A4 inhibitors.
indications:
## Indications

- Nausea/vomiting when benefit outweighs risk.
- Selected adult delayed gastric emptying symptoms.

## Precautions

- **QT prolongation** — not with other QT+ drugs, hypokalemia, HF, potent CYP3A4 inhibitors.
- EMA: lowest dose/shortest duration (usually ≤7 days).

adulto.dose: **10 mg PO up to 3 times/day** (max **30 mg/day**). Prefer ≤7 days.

pediatrico.dose: If specialist indicates: **0.25 mg/kg/dose up to 3/day** (max **0.75 mg/kg/day** or adult **30 mg**).
pediatrico.notes: Consider ondansetron. ECG if risk factors.

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Dry mouth, headache, hyperprolactinemia, QT/arrhythmias, diarrhea.
